one_month_reasoning: Three scheduled supply/information events fall inside 2026-10-13 to 2026-11-12: (1) the staggered early lock-up releases continue (a tranche on Oct 14 and, on the biweekly cadence CNBC reported since Aug 19, another around Oct 28); (2) the main 180-day lock-up (~171M shares per the S-1 summary) ends on the earlier of two trading days after Q3 results or 180 days after the May prospectus, i.e. around Nov 9-13; (3) Q3 results, expected (Earnings Whispers estimate, not yet confirmed by the company) on Wed Nov 11 after the close, so Nov 12 trades on them. Q3 core revenue guide $214-216M already equals consensus $214.7M, so the stock will move on the Q4 guide (consensus $274M), confirmation of 'more than triple revenue in 2027', OpenAI deployment status after the Ultrafast-on-Nvidia report, and GAAP margin/cash burn. Supply overhang argues down; the sharp -24% two-week fall to a post-IPO low, ARK accumulation and bullish Reddit tone argue for some short-term reversal. Net: no directional view; median 147.5 (a hair under spot for lock-up supply) with ~31% one-month log vol (above annual/3.5 baseline because earnings and the main unlock both land in the window).

fair_value.method: Engine-consistent blend at the 2027-10-13 horizon: 7.0x NTM EV/sales on ~$4.73B NTM core revenue ($146.8, w0.5), 50x NTM GAAP-after-SBC earnings ($83.7, w0.3) and a 14.8% WACC DCF to FY2030 with 4% terminal growth ($44.8, w0.2); ~$4.9B net cash at the horizon and 259M diluted shares including the full OpenAI warrant.

Debt $918.2M (F6) - cash $6,742.2M (F1) - ST investments $1,179.4M (F2). Excludes $0.68B restricted cash (conservative) and $568.8M operating lease liabilities (lease cost already inside EBIT).

Peer median EV/sales 22.4x (ttm); peers' median gross margin ~65-75% vs Cerebras 41-43% guide -> gross-profit parity gives ~10x ttm / ~7.5x NTM; a further small discount for capex intensity (30% of revenue in FY28 vs <5% for fabless peers) and single-customer backlog -> 7.0x. methods.inputs: NTM NOPAT (GAAP EBIT after SBC, after NOL-sheltered tax, excluding interest income) ~$433M / 258.8M shares = ~$1.67 x 50x

6M-2026 SBC $386.6M (IPO-triggered RSU vesting); FY2025 SBC $49.8M = 9.8% of revenue; post-IPO ongoing grants assumed ~9% of revenue in FY27, declining with scale.

H1-26 capex $548.9M (147% of revenue) with manufacturing capacity up >10x in 2026 and 600 MW contracted by end-2027 -> ~$1.24B FY26, ~$1.5B FY27, ~$1.6B FY28, then maintenance plus growth.
Hardware inventory build plus receivables from a concentrated customer base; H1-26 operating cash flow -$47.5M despite $386.6M non-cash SBC indicates working capital absorption.
After FY2030 revenue still tied to AI inference demand (above GDP), but SRAM scaling stall and customer concentration argue against more; 4% nominal.

bear.story: OpenAI keeps moving latency-critical inference to Nvidia GPUs or its own silicon (the GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast report is the first sign), backlog conversion slips, Microsoft and other hyperscalers in-source inference, AWS ramp is slow; FY27 revenue ~$2.0B, 4x EV/sales, cash burn continues. Engine bear (deltas -20pt growth, -4pt margin, -2.5x sales multiple, +1pt WACC) gives ~$50-55; I place the centre at $60 because net cash (~$17/share) and the contracted RPO put a floor under the equity.

base.story: Guidance is met (FY26 ~$885M core), FY27 ~$2.7B, FY28 ~$5.3B as the 600-750 MW OpenAI capacity comes online; core op margin turns positive in 2027; the stock re-rates to ~7x NTM sales. Engine base value $107; the price centre is $120 because 12-month prices for hyper-growth AI names have stayed above my fundamental value (spot $148.86, analyst targets ~$300), so I give the market's current premium partial persistence.

bull.story: OpenAI expands toward its 2 GW option, Cerebras regains flagship Ultrafast tiers, AWS Bedrock goes live Q1-2027 and hyperscaler revenue ramps; FY27 ~$3.4B, FY28 >$7B, sales multiple ~11x; close to the street's ~$300 target.

comps_summary.peer_range: Forward P/E 10.2x (SMCI) to 151.5x (ARM), median 39.4x (10 peers; CRWV n/a). EV/EBITDA (trailing, Yahoo; forward EV/EBITDA not available from a reachable public page) 10.6x (SMCI) to 304x (ARM), median 52.4x. EV/sales ttm 0.84x (SMCI) to 68.2x (ARM), median 22.4x.
comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: 7.0x NTM EV/sales vs peer ttm median 22.4x (well inside the range, below median); 50x NTM P/E on GAAP-after-SBC earnings that also exclude interest income, roughly 38-40x on the peers' adjusted basis = at the 39.4x peer median. Cerebras's own EV/sales today ~12x NTM core revenue (EV ~$28B).
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: Discount on EV/sales is structural and persists through the horizon: (a) core gross margin guide 41-43% (FY26) vs ~60-75% for NVDA/AVGO/ALAB/CRDO/ARM, because Cerebras sells delivered capacity from its own data centers; (b) capex at ~30% of revenue in FY28 vs <5% for fabless peers; (c) essentially all of the $25.4B RPO is one customer (OpenAI) that is also its lender and warrant holder. On EV/gross profit the 7x sales multiple is close to parity with the peer median. No premium is applied despite >100% growth because the sell-side's outperformance calls are not admissible and growth is already in NTM revenue.

thesis_break_reason: At $80 the market cap (~$20.6B on 257M diluted shares) less ~$4.9B of projected horizon net cash is an EV of ~$15.5B, about 3x my FY28 revenue and ~60% of RPO: a level that only makes sense if the OpenAI contract is being renegotiated, delayed or partly cancelled (or Cerebras fails to deliver the 600 MW by end-2027). With ~80-100% annual volatility, ordinary noise reaches the $100s; a close below $80 with no market-wide AI sell-off would mean the backlog thesis is broken.

reverse_dcf_check: The engine's reverse DCF says my horizon multiples (7x NTM sales, 50x NTM earnings) imply a WACC of 7.3% on my explicit FY26-FY30 cash flows with 4% terminal growth, against the 14.8% CAPM WACC from a 2.29 peer beta. Put the other way: at 14.8%, the multiples need long-run growth and margins well above my base: roughly revenue compounding ~20%/yr into the mid-2030s (to ~$20B) with 25%+ EBIT margins, i.e. Cerebras taking a durable share of AI inference beyond the OpenAI contract. That is plausible only in the bull case, given the SRAM scaling ceiling, hyperscaler in-sourcing and single-customer backlog (long_dated_risks); it is why I give the DCF 20% weight and keep the sales multiple below the peer median, and why my fair value ($107) sits below spot.

defense_exposure.share_of_revenue: Not separately disclosed; estimated well under 3% (judgment)
defense_exposure.detail: Neither the 424B4 nor the Q2-2026 10-Q quantifies defense/military/intelligence revenue; the prospectus lists national laboratories and defense organizations only as target on-premises customers. Disclosed concentration leaves little room: 2025 revenue was MBZUAI 62% and G42 24% (UAE university and commercial AI group, not military), and in H1-2026 customers A/B/D were 49%/20% (OpenAI ~$74.4M of $373.5M)/10%. The known defense item is a $45M DARPA contract (April 2025) shared with Ranovus for a photonic-interconnect HPC system (RF battlespace emulation), which on any multi-year split is a low-single-digit share of revenue at most. The public job board shows no federal/clearance/defense roles. Civilian government (DOE labs) is separate and also small.

reasoning: Facts: FY26 core revenue guide $880-890M, Q3 guide $214-216M, RPO $25.4B (22% in 24 months, 43% in months 25-48), 600+ MW contracted by end-2027, ~$7.0B net cash (F7), GAAP losses inflated by IPO SBC. Alternative-lane evidence the street has not cut for: SemiAnalysis's X post that OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol Ultrafast runs on Nvidia (Altman later called Cerebras 'a close partner', but the workload was not shown to return); Microsoft Maia in-sourcing; every insider trade in six months a sale (~$240M by CEO/CTO) and a large November unlock; OpenRouter shows Cerebras serving only two models; offsetting: hiring accelerated (37 new postings in September vs 12 in August; 124 open roles, 20 inference-titled), web traffic steady (~1M visits/month), ARK buying >$60M in August, Reddit tone bullish but cooling. No live prediction market on Cerebras exists (the only Polymarket market, on the IPO, has resolved). Valuation: engine-consistent fair value $107 (7x NTM sales $147, 50x NTM GAAP earnings $84, DCF $45 at a 14.8% WACC from the 2.29 peer beta); the reverse DCF shows today's price requires growth beyond the OpenAI backlog. Distribution: lognormal mixture bear 30% @ $60, base 45% @ $120, bull 25% @ $265 (within-scenario vol 0.38-0.45), giving median ~$118, mean ~$149 (about spot) and ~85-95% effective annual vol, below the 115% post-IPO realized vol, in line with high-beta AI peers (betas 1.9-2.9). P(>=spot) ~0.37: I lean below spot on the median because the stock's backlog is one customer that has just been seen routing work elsewhere, while the right tail stays fat. Research limits: X/Reddit pages are not directly fetchable, so social claims were taken via secondary write-ups and labelled; forward EV/EBITDA for peers was not available on a reachable page, so trailing EV/EBITDA is shown; Twelve Data statistics/estimates and Alpha Vantage overview need premium plans and were not used as sources. In-lane share is 13 of 35 sources (37%), below the 60% target, because the mandatory 10-12 peer set needs 11 separate statistics pages plus filings and rate data; excluding those required pages, 13 of 18 are in-lane.
